::: {.callout-warning}
**Use [IBM Verify Counts](ibm_verify_events_transformed.qmd) instead.**
These tables hold one row per event and are kept for 3 years. At full volume
they will grow by hundreds of millions of rows a month. Query them only when no
summary table answers the question, and always filter on the partitions.
:::

The IBM Verify event stream, in the `ibm_verify_events_raw` schema. An hourly
Glue job pulls events from IBM Verify through a proxy in the CanadaLogin platform
account. The proxy hashes every personal identifier before the data leaves that
account. See the [streaming
job](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/ibm_verify_events_streaming/glue_src/ibm_verify_events_streaming_etl.py)
and its [privacy
design](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/docs/ibm-verify-events-streaming/ibm_verify_events_streaming_security_privacy.md),
both in an internal repo.

Data starts at launch, 2026-04-22, except `adaptive_access`, which starts on
2026-09-09.

## Tables

::: {#tables}
:::

## Users

The user ID is `subject` in `authentication_activity` and `mfa_activity`, and
`userid` in `application_usage` and `adaptive_access`. Both hold the same
HMAC-SHA256 digest of the IBM Verify user ID, so they join across tables and
stay stable over time. Count users as distinct values of it.

Exclude null, `""`, and the literal `"UNKNOWN"`. IBM Verify logs `"UNKNOWN"` when
it cannot tie an event to an account, such as a password attempt on a username
that does not exist. The summary tables keep it and count it as one user, to
match IBM's own figures.

`username`, `origin` (the client IP address), and `mfadevice` are hashed the same
way. Countries and regions are not hashed.

## Time and partitions

`time` is a UTC string, for example `2026-09-15 00:00:05 UTC`. The partition
columns `year`, `month`, and `day` are strings for the UTC day.

Always filter on the partitions, which lets Athena skip every other day.
Filtering only on `time` reads the whole table.

Reports use ET days, which end at 04:00 or 05:00 UTC. Read the following UTC day
too, then convert:

```sql
date(with_timezone(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp), 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto')
```

Distinct-user counts do not add up across days. See [Why Unique Users Cannot Be
Added Up](../cookbook/unique-users.qmd).
